category_title: Students who disrupt instruction to avoid difficult independent tasks
student_description: Jay is a third-grade student who uses disruptive behaviors (blurting, bellowing) to avoid independent seatwork when he feels the material is too difficult. He uniquely needs extended guided practice to build confidence and a structured, non-disruptive routine to access teacher support, as punitive measures that result in 1-on-1 help inadvertently reinforce his disruptions.

criteria.rationale: Jay's disruptions are triggered by feeling unprepared for new independent work, so he needs confirmation of understanding before starting.
criteria.check: The tutor extends guided practice, works through an example with him, or explicitly checks his understanding before directing him to work completely independently.

criteria.rationale: Jay needs a functional replacement behavior to access the teacher's help without resorting to bellowing or blurting.
criteria.check: The tutor offers or reminds Jay of a specific, non-disruptive way to get help (e.g., moving to a back table, raising a hand, using a help card).

criteria.rationale: Punitive measures that result in 1-on-1 teacher time reinforce Jay's avoidance behavior by giving him exactly what he wants.
criteria.check: The tutor does not threaten or apply a punishment (such as losing recess or free time) that involves keeping Jay in to do the work with 1-on-1 teacher support.
